newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia's Howard sees more bank competition.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia's Howard sees more bank competition.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday he hoped the government's financial industry inquiry would result in more competition among banks.
"I believe that one of the things that we've got to look for out of this Wallis inquiry, and wE'll have that in a couple of months, iS more competition," Howard told Sydney radio 2UE.
Howard said competition would help reduce interest rates for business loans.
"Housing loans now are much lower than small business loans and they're much lower than they've been for years. You know why? Because of competition," he said.
The Liberal-National government set up an inquiry into the finance sector, headed by businessman Stan Wallis, soon after its March election.

A major issue for the inquiry is to address whether mergers should be allowed between the big four banks: the National Australia Bank Ltd, Westpac Banking Corp, AUstralia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia Ltd.
The Wallis inquiry is due to conclude by March, but a draft report is due to be ready this month.
